description: 6-axis compound identity taxonomy for Kinetic property classification. Each property receives one tag per axis, producing a unique cohort fingerprint that governs E.V.O. fleet intelligence, territorial exclusivity, and protocol sequencing.

_field_conventions.id: Stable machine-readable identifier. NEVER rename once a property has been tagged.
_field_conventions.label: Human-readable display name.
_field_conventions.description: Contextual explanation used in onboarding and diagnostic reports.
_field_conventions.categories: Axis 1 only. Groups business models into higher-order families for cohort clustering.
_field_conventions.range: Axis 2 only. Page count boundaries that define the tier.
_field_conventions.signals: Observable indicators E.V.O. uses to auto-classify a property on this axis.

axes.label: Business Model
axes.description: The fundamental commercial archetype of the property. Determines content strategy patterns, conversion topology, and which keyword intent distributions are structurally relevant.

categories.label: Service-Based
categories.description: Revenue from human-delivered services. SEO patterns center on local intent, trust signals, and service area coverage.

models.label: Local Service Business
models.description: Single-location service provider. SEO dominated by local pack, GBP optimization, and geo-modified keywords.

models.label: Multi-Location Service
models.description: Service provider operating across multiple geographic locations. SEO requires location page architecture and cross-location authority distribution.

models.label: Professional Services / B2B
models.description: High-consideration B2B services (legal, consulting, finance). Long sales cycles with thought leadership content as primary organic driver.

models.label: Agency / Consultancy
models.description: Client services firm selling expertise. Portfolio-driven trust building with content marketing as lead generation engine.

categories.label: Product-Based
categories.description: Revenue from physical or digital product sales. SEO patterns center on product discovery, category architecture, and transactional intent capture.

models.label: E-commerce (Small)
models.description: Small-catalog online store. SEO focused on product page optimization, long-tail product keywords, and category page authority.

models.label: E-commerce (Enterprise)
models.description: Large-catalog enterprise commerce. SEO challenges include faceted navigation, crawl budget management, and duplicate content at scale.

models.label: D2C Brand
models.description: Direct-to-consumer brand selling owned products. SEO blends branded search defense with editorial content for top-of-funnel discovery.

models.label: Marketplace / Aggregator
models.description: Platform connecting buyers and sellers or aggregating listings. SEO driven by programmatic page generation and UGC indexation.

categories.label: Content-Based
categories.description: Revenue from content monetization (ads, subscriptions, lead generation). SEO is the primary revenue driver, not a support channel.

models.label: Publisher / Media
models.description: Content publisher monetizing through ads, subscriptions, or sponsorships. SEO patterns emphasize freshness, topical authority, and news indexing.

models.label: Blog-Driven SaaS
models.description: SaaS product using content marketing as primary acquisition channel. Blog content targets informational keywords that funnel to product pages.
signals: blog subdirectory with high page count

models.label: Knowledge Base / Documentation
models.description: Structured reference content (docs, wikis, help centers). SEO value in long-tail technical queries and developer search intent.

models.label: Directory / Listing Site
models.description: Structured directory of entities (businesses, products, people). SEO driven by programmatic templates and aggregated authority.

categories.label: SaaS / Technology
categories.description: Software products sold as subscriptions. SEO patterns vary dramatically by stage — from brand building to category defense.

models.label: SaaS (Early Stage)
models.description: Pre-PMF or early-growth SaaS. SEO focused on category definition, competitor comparison captures, and foundational technical health.

models.label: SaaS (Growth)
models.description: Growth-stage SaaS scaling organic acquisition. SEO expanding into content hubs, feature pages, and integration/ecosystem content.

models.label: SaaS (Enterprise)
models.description: Mature enterprise SaaS defending category position. SEO focused on branded SERP control, competitor defense, and thought leadership authority.

models.label: Developer Tools / API-First
models.description: Products targeting developers. SEO uniquely driven by documentation quality, GitHub presence, and technical content that doubles as product education.

axes.label: Scale Tier
axes.description: The property's indexed footprint size. Determines crawl budget dynamics, internal linking complexity, and which architectural patterns are structurally necessary vs. premature optimization.

tiers.label: Micro
tiers.description: Minimal indexed footprint. Every page is hand-crafted. SEO wins come from precision optimization of individual pages rather than structural architecture.

tiers.label: Small
tiers.description: Small but structured footprint. Category/tag architecture becomes relevant. Internal linking strategy starts to matter.

tiers.label: Medium
tiers.description: Substantial footprint requiring deliberate architecture. Crawl budget awareness needed. Content cannibalization risk emerges. Programmatic patterns may be present.

tiers.label: Large
tiers.description: Large footprint where architectural decisions dominate SEO outcomes. Crawl budget is a primary constraint. Index bloat is an active threat. Programmatic generation likely.

tiers.label: Massive
tiers.description: Massive footprint where SEO is fundamentally an information architecture and crawl engineering problem. Page-level optimization is irrelevant; system-level patterns determine outcomes.

axes.label: Tech Architecture
axes.description: The rendering and delivery architecture of the property. Determines which technical SEO patterns are relevant, what crawl/render issues to expect, and which diagnostic protocols apply.

profiles.label: Static HTML / Traditional CMS
profiles.description: Server-rendered HTML (WordPress, Drupal, Joomla, static HTML). Crawling is straightforward. SEO issues are typically content and structural, not rendering-related.

profiles.label: JavaScript SPA (React, Vue, Angular)
profiles.description: Client-side rendered single-page application. SEO challenges include render-dependent indexing, JavaScript crawl budget, hydration issues, and dynamic routing.

profiles.label: Headless CMS + SSR/SSG
profiles.description: Decoupled architecture with server-side rendering or static site generation. Best-of-both: modern frontend with crawl-friendly HTML output. SEO challenges shift to build pipeline and cache invalidation.

profiles.label: Shopify Hydrogen / Hosted E-commerce
profiles.description: Managed e-commerce platform with custom or semi-custom frontend. SEO constrained by platform capabilities — URL structure, schema markup, and rendering are partially platform-controlled.

profiles.label: Custom Framework
profiles.description: Bespoke or proprietary architecture. SEO diagnostics cannot rely on platform-specific heuristics. Requires first-principles technical analysis of rendering, routing, and crawlability.

axes.label: SEO Maturity
axes.description: The property's current position on the SEO capability curve. Determines which protocols are relevant, what level of optimization is premature, and where the highest-leverage interventions exist.

stages.label: Unoptimized
stages.description: No deliberate SEO work has been done. Technical foundations are absent or broken. The opportunity surface is maximal — almost any intervention produces measurable improvement.

stages.label: Foundation Built
stages.description: Basic technical SEO is in place. Site is crawlable and indexed. Optimization is shallow — default CMS settings, minimal schema, no content strategy. Ready for strategic buildout.

stages.label: Technically Sound
stages.description: Technical SEO is solid. Core Web Vitals passing. Schema implemented. The bottleneck shifts from technical health to content strategy and authority building.

stages.label: Growth Phase
stages.description: Active SEO growth. Content clusters expanding. Backlinks growing. Organic traffic on an upward trajectory. Optimization focus shifts to efficiency — maximizing output per input.

stages.label: Mature / Defending
stages.description: Category leader or established authority. Organic traffic is substantial. The strategic challenge shifts from growth to defense — protecting rankings, preventing decay, and identifying diminishing returns.

axes.label: Geographic Profile
axes.description: The property's geographic and linguistic targeting scope. Determines hreflang complexity, local SEO relevance, international indexing strategy, and which geographic patterns E.V.O. should monitor.

profiles.label: Single Market, Single Language
profiles.description: One country, one language. The simplest geographic profile. SEO is focused entirely on one search index. Local SEO may or may not be relevant depending on business model.

profiles.label: Single Market, Multi-Language
profiles.description: One country, multiple languages (e.g., Canada EN/FR, Switzerland DE/FR/IT). Requires hreflang implementation within a single market. Content duplication management is critical.
seo_implications: potential thin content if translations are shallow

profiles.label: Multi-Market, Single Language
profiles.description: Multiple countries, one language (e.g., US + UK + AU in English). Requires geo-targeting strategy — ccTLDs, subdirectories, or subdomains — without translation complexity.
signals: hreflang with same language different regions

profiles.label: Global, Multi-Language
profiles.description: Multiple countries, multiple languages. Maximum international SEO complexity. Requires comprehensive hreflang graph, market-specific content strategy, and cross-market authority architecture.

axes.label: Content Velocity
axes.description: The rate at which the property publishes new indexable content. Determines freshness signals, crawl frequency expectations, content decay risk, and whether the SEO strategy is stock-based or flow-based.

velocities.label: Static
velocities.description: Content rarely changes. Pages are published once and left. SEO is entirely stock-based — the existing corpus must carry all organic performance. Content decay is the primary long-term risk.
seo_implications: existing pages must be maximally optimized
internal linking is the main lever
refreshing old content > creating new content

velocities.label: Low
velocities.description: Occasional content publication. Enough to signal freshness but not enough to build momentum. SEO strategy must be highly selective — every piece of content must count.
seo_implications: every post must target high-value terms

velocities.label: Moderate
velocities.description: Consistent content cadence. Enough to build topical clusters over time. SEO strategy can be systematic — pillar/spoke models, editorial calendars, and content hub expansion.

velocities.label: High
velocities.description: Aggressive content publication. Rapid footprint expansion. SEO must manage quality at volume — content governance, cannibalization detection, and crawl budget become active concerns.

velocities.label: Programmatic
velocities.description: Content generated at scale through templates, data pipelines, or AI systems. Hundreds or thousands of pages created systematically. SEO is fundamentally an architecture and quality control problem.
seo_implications: unique value per page must be enforced
Google's helpful content signals are primary constraint
crawl budget is a first-class architectural concern

_compound_identity_format.description: A property's compound identity is expressed as a 6-tuple of axis IDs, providing a unique cohort fingerprint for fleet intelligence and territorial exclusivity.
_compound_identity_format.example_readable: Growth-stage SaaS | Medium footprint (1K-10K pages) | Headless CMS + SSR/SSG | Growth Phase maturity | Single market, single language | Moderate content velocity

_territorial_exclusivity_note: Within the Kinetic fleet, no two properties may occupy the same compound identity AND compete for overlapping primary keyword clusters in the same geographic market. E.V.O. performs competitive overlap analysis at onboarding to enforce this constraint.
_intelligence_contribution_note: Every property's diagnostic cycles, protocol completions, and outcome data are attributed to its compound identity. Fleet intelligence accumulates per cohort region, enabling E.V.O. to transfer learned patterns — fingerprint correlations, protocol sequencing, cascade predictions — to new properties sharing the same or adjacent compound identities.
